description: Pozole Rojo is a hearty and flavorful Mexican soup, a true celebration in a bowl. Made with tender pork, hominy kernels, and a rich, spicy red chile broth, it's a dish deeply rooted in tradition and perfect for sharing. This vibrant and comforting stew offers a complex blend of savory and mildly spicy notes, making it a beloved staple for gatherings and holidays.

ingredients.notes: one half quartered, one half roughly chopped

instructions.title: Cook the Pork
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, combine the pork shoulder, one quartered onion half, 3 whole garlic cloves, 1 tablespoon salt, peppercorns, and bay leaves. Cover with enough water or chicken broth to submerge the pork by about 2 inches. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes, or until the pork is very tender and easily shredded.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chile Sauce
instructions.text: While the pork cooks, rehydrate the dried chiles. Place the guajillo and ancho chiles in a heatproof bowl and cover them with hot water. Let them soak for 20-30 minutes until they are soft and pliable. Drain the chiles, reserving about 1 cup of the soaking liquid.

instructions.title: Blend the Chile Sauce
instructions.text: In a blender, combine the rehydrated chiles, the remaining roughly chopped onion half, 3 minced garlic cloves, Mexican oregano, and ground cumin. Add about 1/2 cup of the reserved chile soaking liquid or fresh water. Blend until the mixture is completely smooth. For a silky texture, strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, pressing with a spoon to extract all the liquid. Discard any solids remaining in the sieve.

instructions.title: Combine and Simmer
instructions.text: Remove the cooked pork from the pot and shred it using two forks. Discard the cooked onion, garlic, peppercorns, and bay leaves from the cooking liquid. Skim any excess fat from the broth if desired. Return the shredded pork to the pot with the broth. Add the drained and rinsed hominy and the strained red chile sauce. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.

instructions.title: Develop Flavors
instructions.text: Continue to simmer the pozole for another 30-45 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing all the flavors to meld and deepen. This simmering time helps the broth absorb the rich chile flavors and slightly thicken. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt if needed. The broth should turn a beautiful rich red color.

instructions.title: Serve with Toppings
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Pozole Rojo into individual bowls. Serve immediately with a variety of traditional toppings on the side for guests to customize their bowls. Popular options include shredded cabbage, thinly sliced radishes, finely diced white onion, fresh lime wedges, and crispy tostadas. You can also offer a dollop of Mexican crema or avocado slices.

tips: For a truly authentic taste, always use dried Mexican chiles (guajillo and ancho) and rehydrate them properly. Do not substitute with chile powder.
If you prefer a thicker broth, you can blend a small amount of hominy with the chile sauce to add more body to the soup.

Pozole Rojo tastes even better the next day! Prepare it in advance and reheat gently for a deeper, more developed flavor. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
